cohort: The cohort consisted of 775 fathers with at least one child aged 3-12 months, recruited via an online survey during the COVID-19 pandemic.
finding: Paternal depression, relationship satisfaction, COVID-19-related psychological distress, and social support significantly affected father-to-infant attachment, with paternal depression being the most influential factor.
mod_finding: No significant association between delivery mode and father-to-infant attachment was observed.
cross-section timing: Data was collected between June and December 2021, when infants were 3-12 months postpartum.
